docs.title: Sankhara
docs.text:
Sankhara is a turn-based world game played on a procedurally generated hex map. You are born into a family on a tile of the world, act each turn, and those actions shape your health and karma — and, eventually, what you are reborn as.

The name comes from the Pali saṅkhāra: the mental formations and volitional impulses that, in Buddhist thought, condition what comes next. See Concepts.

Status

Early prototype. Map generation, resources, a basic player/family model and turn actions exist; karma, NPCs and terrain are still stubs.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
uv sync
uv run sankhara        # or: uv run python -m sankhara

From the main menu choose New Game, click a tile to inspect it, and use the info panel to start a life and take actions.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
All code lives in the sankhara package under src/.

Package Responsibility sankhara.constants config.py: every tunable value — noise parameters, map size, biome thresholds and resource baselines, player actions, culture groups. sankhara.world Map generation (map_gen.py), hex-grid math (hexgrid.py) and resource extraction/regeneration (resources.py). sankhara.core game_engine.generate_map(seed) builds the map; day_plan enforces the 24-hour action budget; turn_manager applies end-of-day resource regeneration and action effects. sankhara.entities Player, PlayerState, Family (lineage) and name generation. sankhara.ui Kivy widgets: the info/action panel (ui_kivy.py), screens (menu, map view, game over), text formatters (screens/info_panel.py) and the palette, biome colours and styled widgets (theme.py). sankhara.app SankharaApp and the screen manager wiring; main() is the entry point.

docs.title: World generation
docs.text:
1. Perlin noise (noise library) produces elevation and moisture grids of MAP_WIDTH × MAP_HEIGHT, normalised to [0, 1]. Each new game picks a random seed (shown in the panel header); the same seed always gives the same map. Noise is sampled at each hex's true position so features aren't stretched by the offset layout.
  2. Each value is bucketed by ELEVATION_THRESHOLDS / MOISTURE_THRESHOLDS; the pair names the biome (e.g. "Hill Forest").
  3. Resources are seeded from BIOME_RESOURCE_BASELINES with ± RESOURCE_VARIATION_PERCENTAGE random variation.

The map is a list of columns of tile dicts with id, q (column), r (row), elevation, moisture, biome, abbr and resources.

docs.title: Hex grid
docs.text: world/hexgrid.py is pure math for a pointy-top grid in "odd-r" offset coordinates (odd rows shifted half a hex right). tile_center, pixel_to_tile (exact, via cube rounding), hex_corners and fit_size are all the map view needs: it fits the map to its widget, draws row 0 at the top, and hit-tests clicks. Biome fill colours come from theme.biome_color, which derives hue from the moisture band and shading from the elevation band.

docs.title: Day loop
docs.text: Each turn is a day. The player fills up to four action slots; day_plan only offers actions that fit in the hours left (24 per day) and respects non-repeatable actions. On End Day, process_player_actions() applies each taken action's karma and health effects (once per occurrence), applies skip penalties for skippable actions not taken, clamps karma to [-1, 1] and health to [0, 100], and returns the effects, which the panel writes to its log. regenerate_resources() regrows renewable resources toward their biome maximum. When health reaches 0 the game-over screen shows a summary of the life.

docs.title: Stubs
docs.text: core/karma.py, entities/npc.py, world/terrain.py and world/biomes.py are empty placeholders for planned features.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The game's mechanics are meant to model a handful of Buddhist ideas. This page is a skeleton to be expanded from the original design conversation.

docs.title: Saṅkhāra
docs.text: Mental formations or volitional impulses: one of the five aggregates and the second link of dependent origination. In the game, the accumulated effect of a character's choices.

docs.title: Karma
docs.text: Intentional action and its consequences. Each turn's actions (and skipped obligations) adjust a karma score clamped to [-1, 1]; see ACTIONS in sankhara/constants/config.py.

docs.title: Rebirth and lineage
docs.text: A player is born into a Family on a home tile, which determines their culture group and names. Player.reincarnate() swaps in a new state (and optionally a new family); how karma drives rebirth is still to be designed.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• How karma maps to the next birth (species, family, location).
  • Whether NPCs share the same karma model.

docs.title: User Notes
docs.text:
• Original conversation is lost.
  • The game overall is supposed to be a nation builder that does not focus on war and army building. It's supposed to be a strategy game with resource mangament, policy/government management, scientific and cultural development but without armies and war being the main goal.
  • The Karma and rebirth cycle was inspired by the mechanics of the leader in games like Europa Universalis, in which the player is in charge of a country, but the leaders are born and die throughout the game, and lineage is an import aspect of holding power.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Requires uv. The project is pinned to Python 3.12 (.python-version); uv will download it if needed.

uv sync                     # create .venv with runtime + dev dependencies
uv run pre-commit install   # run ruff and basic checks on every commit

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text: Task Command Run the game uv run sankhara Tests (with coverage) uv run pytest Lint uv run ruff check . Format uv run ruff format . All pre-commit hooks uv run pre-commit run --all-files Docs preview uv run --group docs mkdocs serve

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Tests live in tests/, mirroring the package layout (test_core/, test_world/, …). tests/conftest.py sets KIVY_NO_ARGS so Kivy doesn't consume pytest's arguments. UI tests need a display; CI runs them under xvfb-run.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: GitHub Actions runs lint and tests on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/ci.yml), and publishes these docs to GitHub Pages on pushes to main (.github/workflows/docs.yml).
